name: Frame Energy
description: Measures total pixel intensity variance across video frames to detect energy distribution anomalies arising from temporal incoherence in independently generated or interpolated video frames.
mechanism:
This method analyzes total frame energy for video forensic detection:

1. **Frame Energy Computation**: Total frame energy is computed as E = Σ I(x,y)² over all pixels, along with AC energy (energy excluding DC component, measuring content energy). Per-region energy (face, background, edges, smooth areas) provides a spatial energy map.

2. **Temporal Energy Profile**: Frame energy is tracked across time. Natural video shows smooth energy evolution with changes correlated to content (brighter scenes = higher energy, more texture = higher AC energy). Deepfakes may produce energy profiles with anomalous micro-fluctuations from frame-independent generation.

3. **Channel Energy Distribution**: Energy distribution across color channels (R, G, B) should be consistent with scene illumination. The method measures per-channel energy ratios. Deepfake face insertion may alter channel energy distribution in the face region relative to the background.

4. **Frequency-Band Energy Partition**: Frame energy is decomposed into frequency bands (low, medium, high frequency). Natural images partition energy predictably with approximately 1/f spectral character. AI-generated content may show anomalous energy in specific frequency bands — excess energy at the generator's characteristic frequencies or insufficient high-frequency energy.

5. **Energy Consistency Scoring**: The temporal stability of energy, spatial coherence of energy distribution, and conformity to natural image energy statistics are combined into a forensic score. Systematic energy anomalies — particularly between face regions and surrounding content — indicate manipulation.
parameters:
Analysis type: statistical
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through frame energy analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video

references.title: Zheng, Y. et al. (2021). Exploring Temporal Coherence for More General Video Face Forgery Detection. ICCV.
Verdoliva, L. (2020). Media Forensics and DeepFakes: An Overview. IEEE JSTSP.
